dedupe_keys.name: household pulse survey and household trends and outlook pulse survey hps htops

description: The Household Pulse Survey (HPS) is a rapid-response survey run by the U.S. Census Bureau with other federal agencies to measure how emergent issues affect U.S. households. Launched in April 2020, it collected cross-sectional data until 16 September 2024; in January 2025 it relaunched within the Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey (HTOPS), which was longitudinal through 2025 and cross-sectional from March 2026. Topics relevant to infrastructure include household energy use and spending, cooling devices at home, keeping the home at a safe temperature on hot days, actions to reduce cooling costs, available transport options and access to transport, as in the July 2026 tables; earlier waves covered displacement by natural disasters, difficulty paying energy bills, and internet use. Coverage: the United States with national and, in the cross-sectional years, state and metropolitan estimates; the latest release collected 15 July to 3 August 2026. Access: detailed tables and standard error tables (XLSX), Public Use Files with replicate weights (CSV), and an interactive data tool; free and public domain. Caveats: experimental, with low response rates and questions that change between waves, so topics are not continuous; the March and May 2026 PUF weights were corrected on 10 September 2026. Simulation uses: behavioural and social inputs for heat, outage and disaster displacement studies, energy insecurity analysis and transport access. Related records: CRE for Heat, Local Air Conditioning Estimates and EIA's RECS.
